newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF licenses insurance firms for turf change.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF licenses insurance firms for turf change.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Tuesday it had given 17 life and non-life insurance companies licences to do business in each other's turf through subsidiaries.
But a MOF official said licences for products in the so-called "third sector", which includes such cover as accident and health insurance, had conditions attached.

"We may put certain conditions to allow (non-life and life insurance subsidiaries) to do some third-sector business by September 30...in order to avoid any radical changes in the business environment," he said.

The ministry may work out conditions on the entry of domestic insurance firms' subsidiaries into the third sector before the units start new business on October 1, as some of third-sector business could jeopardise smaller insurers and foreign insurers in Japan, the official said.
An amendment to the law that took effect in April allows insurers to conduct both life and non-life insurance business through subsidiaries.
Earlier this month, 11 Japanese non-life and six life insurance companies submitted applications to the ministry to start operating in each other's turf.
The official said life insurance firms' non-life arms should post profits in 10 years, and non-life insurers' life insurance units should do so within 15 years.

Washington and Tokyo have been at odds over the entry of Japanese insurers' subsidiaries into the third-sector niche market, particularly accident insurance. Foreign insurers have a strong market position in the third sector.
Several rounds of talks have been held to resolve the situation, and new talks are due in September.
The MOF official said no exact schedule for the talks had yet been set.
